newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Plan to save Kia Group.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Plan to save Kia Group.

text.p: The Kia Group bailout may leave a sour taste in some bankers' mouths, as they embark on their third rescue of a Korean corporate this year.
Bankers said Korean banks had agreed to bail out Kia Group, the country's eighth largest business conglomerate.
The Bank of Korea plans to release money through repurchase agreements to prevent tight short-term liquidity.

"We plan to provide one trillion won to the banking system in view of possible tight liquidity following the application by Kia Group for protection against debt repayment defaults," a Bank of Korea official said.
The bank official said some banks were having difficult meeting reserve requirements as a result of tight money supply.
Despite the well publicised bank bailouts of Korean corporates, banks are still interested in Korean bank paper, particular shorter term or featuring puts and calls.
Cho Hung Bank's one-year floating-rate note (FRN) is priced at par to float at 40 basis points over six month London Interbank Offered Rate, offering participants an all-in of 52 basis points.
Pusan Bank's US$60 million three-year FRN through BA (Asia) is priced at par to float at 50 basis points over three-month LIBOR, and features annual puts and calls.
In other news, Hong Kong's Airport Authority (AA) has set its HK$3.0 billion revolving credit facility.
It said it had mandated China Development Finance Co (Hong Kong) Ltd, Tokyo-Mitsubishi International (HK), Chase Manhattan Asia Ltd and HSBC Investment Bank Asia to arrange the deal.
CDFC and Chase Manhattan Bank are the bookrunners.
The AA said the facility will pay a margin of 30 basis points per annum plus fees, which have not been disclosed.
China Merchant Bank has set its US$100 million seven-year FRN through SBC Warburg.
Issue price was par, and the coupon was 70 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate, for an all-in of 78.6 basis points.
Bankers liked the all-in, saying it was in line with the 75 basis point to 80 basis point average for five-year paper -- the deal features puts and calls at year five.

Bankers expect Agricultural Bank of China's US$120 million five-year floating-rate certificate of deposit issue through its Singapore branch to pay an all-in in the low "30's", when arrangers SocGen Asia and Bayerische Landesbank.
Asia Pacific Resources International Holdings Ltd's subsidiary, P.T. Riau Pulp & Paper has launched an offer to repurchase outstanding notes.

It is offering to buy back all outstanding 11-1/2 percent guaranteed secured notes due 2000 and all 13-1/4 percent guaranteed secured notes due 2005 issued by its subsidiary RAPP International Finance Co BV.
